title: The semi-representable object of maps from a finite simplicial set
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme with small etale site $X_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], let $K$ be a simplicial object of the category $\mathrm{SR}(X)$ of semi-representable objects over $X$ [def-weil-pbc-semi-representable-object], with operators $K(\varphi):K_n\to K_m$ for $\varphi:[m]\to[n]$ in the category $\Delta$ of [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set], and let $S$ be a simplicial set [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set] with $S_n$ finite and nonempty for all $n\geq0$ and with finitely many nondegenerate simplices. For an object $W$ of $\mathrm{SR}(X)$, an *$S$-family in $K$ over $W$* is a family of morphisms $f_s:W\to K_n$ of $\mathrm{SR}(X)$, one for each $n\geq0$ and $s\in S_n$, with $K(\varphi)\circ f_s=f_{S(\varphi)(s)}$ for every $\varphi:[m]\to[n]$ and $s\in S_n$. For a morphism $g:W'\to W$ of $\mathrm{SR}(X)$ and an $S$-family $(f_s)$ over $W$, $(f_s\circ g)_s$ is an $S$-family over $W'$ (compose the defining equations with $g$); with the identities and the associativity of composition in $\mathrm{SR}(X)$ this makes $\mathcal F_{S,K}:W\mapsto\{S\text{-families in }K\text{ over }W\}$, $g\mapsto((f_s)\mapsto(f_s\circ g))$, a functor $\mathrm{SR}(X)^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathrm{Sets}$. An object $\operatorname{Hom}(S,K)_0$ of $\mathrm{SR}(X)$ with an $S$-family $(u_s)$ over it is any pair representing $\mathcal F_{S,K}$ with universal object $(u_s)$ [def-weil-pbc-representing-object]: for every object $W$ of $\mathrm{SR}(X)$, $g\mapsto(u_s\circ g)_s$ is a bijection from the morphisms $W\to\operatorname{Hom}(S,K)_0$ to the $S$-families over $W$. Such a pair exists by [lem-weil-pbc-simplicial-hom-object-exists]; one is fixed. In particular, for an object $T$ of $X_{\Et}$ the $T$-points of $\operatorname{Hom}(S,K)_0$ (morphisms $\{T\}\to\operatorname{Hom}(S,K)_0$ [def-weil-pbc-semi-representable-object]) correspond by $g\mapsto(u_s\circ g)_s$ to the $S$-families over $\{T\}$: the families $(f_s)$ of $T$-points $f_s$ of $K_n$, one for each $n\geq0$ and $s\in S_n$, with $K(\varphi)\circ f_s=f_{S(\varphi)(s)}$. Let $A\subseteq S$ be a simplicial subset [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set] satisfying the same hypotheses ($A_n$ finite and nonempty for all $n$, finitely many nondegenerate simplices), with its own fixed $(\operatorname{Hom}(A,K)_0,(u^A_s)_{s\in A})$, and write $(u^S_s)$ for the universal family of $\operatorname{Hom}(S,K)_0$. Since the operators of $A$ are the restrictions of those of $S$, $(u^S_s)_{s\in A}$ is an $A$-family over $\operatorname{Hom}(S,K)_0$; the *restriction morphism* $\rho:\operatorname{Hom}(S,K)_0\to\operatorname{Hom}(A,K)_0$ is the unique morphism with $u^A_s\circ\rho=u^S_s$ for all simplices $s$ of $A$, which exists and is unique by the universal property of $\operatorname{Hom}(A,K)_0$. Likewise restriction $(f_s)_{s\in S}\mapsto(f_s)_{s\in A}$ sends $S$-families over $W$ to $A$-families over $W$, compatibly with composition, and corresponds to $g\mapsto\rho\circ g$.

split_report.summary: Read Stacks simplicial.tex 017H/017I/017J/017K and categories.tex 001Q. Definition split: the statement now names every notion it is built from: the small etale site (def-weil-pbc-etale-site, for T and {T}), SR(X), its T-points and simplicial objects of SR(X) (def-weil-pbc-semi-representable-object), Delta, simplicial sets, nondegenerate simplices and simplicial subsets (def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set, Mathlib leaf), and the new Mathlib leaf def-weil-pbc-representing-object (object representing a presheaf of sets with universal object, Stacks 001Q; CategoryTheory.Functor.IsRepresentedBy). The functor of S-families is written out (functoriality by composition), Hom(S,K)_0 is any pair representing it (Stacks 017I: 'we denote Hom(U,V) any ...'), existence is taken by name from lem-weil-pbc-simplicial-hom-object-exists (017K). Changes to the statement: removed the parenthetical claim that S-families are the morphisms of simplicial objects W x S -> K (it is the first paragraph of the proof of 017J, needs coproducts in SR(X), and no citer uses it) and the claim 'unique up to unique isomorphism' (a claim inside a definition, not used by the citers); the restriction morphism now says why (u^S_s)_{s in A} is an A-family and that rho exists uniquely by the universal property of Hom(A,K)_0. No slopmaster2 Lean exists for this notion.
split_report.blueprint: The definition serves lem-weil-pbc-hypercover-refinement, proof, fourth paragraph ('Previously chosen faces prescribe compatible boundaries; the matching covers of U lift those boundaries after finite refinement'): Hom(S,K)_0 is the object of compatible boundary data on a finite simplicial set S, its T-points are the compatible boundaries, and the restriction morphism Hom(B,K)_0 -> Hom(A,K)_0 is the map from lifts to boundaries that lem-weil-pbc-hypercover-finite-simplex-lifting shows is a covering.
